can_answer: yes for the year-by-year composition of recorded motorist-plus-cyclist deaths; this does not describe their share of all traffic deaths
metric: For each calendar year, the share of the combined motorist and cyclist death count attributable to motorists and to cyclists, calculated separately
denominator: For each year, the sum of number_of_motorist_killed and number_of_cyclist_killed; the two displayed group shares sum to 100% when this denominator is positive
population: Police-reported NYC motor vehicle crashes dated 2013-01-01 through 2025-12-31; motorist and cyclist deaths in those crashes
filters: crash_date year from 2013 through 2025 inclusive; no borough or location filter
grouping: Calendar year and road-user group (motorist, cyclist)
data_check_interpretation: The selected population contains 2,132,218 crash records (per-year row counts are in check_2.csv). The crash_date range is 2013-01-01 through 2025-12-31, with observed date extents covering Jan 1-Dec 31 in every included year. Within this filtered population, crash_date missing/default/out-of-range counts are all zero; because the year filter itself requires a valid in-range date, rows with missing or out-of-range dates are not part of this population and cannot be counted by this check. Both death columns used in the numerator and denominator have zero missing values overall and in every year. Keep all rows; no data-check-based exclusions or imputations are needed. The denominator intentionally consists only of motorist and cyclist deaths, so deaths among other road users are outside this comparison. Full observed date extents do not prove reporting completeness.
limitations: Shares compare only motorists with cyclists, not either group's share of all traffic deaths, and are not population- or exposure-adjusted risks; full observed date extents do not establish reporting completeness.
